title: External Technician · BBS field operations
subtitle: Authorized own work, expenses, reports, corrections and supplier operational evidence

chapters.title: Start with authorized supplier access
chapters.context: Isolated BBS supplier role lab · genuine External Technician account · fictional October 2026 records
paragraphs: Use the individual External Technician account created or invited by the Owner. There is no public sign-up. Account activity, supplier association, supplier project authorization and your project assignment must all cover the work date. A supplier coordinator is a different role and may record team work; that does not let you see another technician’s sources.

This course uses BBS ROLE LAB External Technician in the isolated C-0050-P-20261005 · BBS · Ejemplo de manual project. New work is fictional, outside the original billed October 2–5 history. The supplier authorization covers October 5–31. No live dispatch, purchase, equipment change or bank transfer occurred.

Before practising obtain an operator-provided training URL, own account, visible environment identifier, permitted scope and reset instructions. No shared training credentials are supplied. Live company portal or webmail links open live services, never this isolated demonstration.
steps: Sign in with your own account and verify environment, account and language.
Use Time for your own hours, Expenses for your own operational purchases, Reports for your own Daily/Technical facts and Operational report for your allowed activity summary.
Use Profile and Help for own workforce/security settings and guidance.
checks: Your assigned BBS project is available. Finance, Billing, My Pay and supplier team administration are outside this role.
recovery: Ask the Owner/coordinator to investigate account, supplier authorization or assignment dates when the intended project is absent. Do not borrow an account or create duplicate work.

chapters.title: First shift: save actual time, then submit
chapters.context: Native isolated BBS role exercise · C-0050-P-20261005 · synthetic October 2026 work only
paragraphs: Begin with your own assigned project and actual work. Published plans and expected hours are planning information; neither creates time. The October 13 example records fictional documentation work, not a real dispatch.

A draft remains editable. Submit only after checking project, work date, duration and activity. Submission sends supplier time to Owner review and locks ordinary editing. See Review authority · who receives each source (review-authority) and Recovery · sources, obligations and immutable history (recovery-matrix).
steps: Open Time and choose Log time. Select BBS, Work date 2026-10-13, Category Regular time, Duration in hours 1.25 and a precise synthetic activity summary.
Check any site, shift or break fields against the actual work. Choose Save draft and wait for the saved result; a Saving label is a transient state.
Open the saved source, confirm 1.25 h and Draft, then choose Submit. Verify Submitted on that source.
checks: Native Save draft and Submit succeeded. Original source 01a11176-38c3-713d-92a2-e4f5ab3d9240 was later returned for correction; its current state is Needs changes.
recovery: If save fails, correct the visible validation error and verify whether a source was created before retrying. Never create a duplicate to replace a submitted source.

chapters.title: Correct returned time and verify Owner approval
chapters.route: Time → returned source → Create corrected draft
chapters.context: Native isolated BBS role exercise · C-0050-P-20261005 · synthetic October 2026 work only
paragraphs: Needs changes preserves the submitted source and reviewer reason. A correction creates a linked replacement; it does not silently overwrite approved or submitted history.
The October 13 original records 1.25 h. Owner requested one actual hour; the replacement records 1 h. The original remains Needs changes and the replacement is Approved.
steps: Open the returned source and read the reason. Choose Create corrected draft.
Confirm date, category and actual duration; write the corrected activity and Reason for correction. Choose Create correction draft.

Check the linked draft and original link. Submit individually or include the eligible draft in Submit this week. After Owner review, reopen the replacement and verify Approved and its approved timestamp.
checks: Correction 01a1117a-6cef-7576-900b-329b43e9ecb0 is Approved; the saved linked original remains visible. The isolated audit also verified Owner as the recorded approver. The source screen shows the approval timestamp, rather than a reviewer-name field.
recovery: If a reason remains unclear, ask the Owner/coordinator before submitting. An explanation does not itself change review state.

figures.caption: Actual linked correction form with corrected duration and reason.
Actual October 13 linked replacement: Approved, 1 h, original link and approval timestamp.

chapters.title: Review a week and submit eligible drafts
chapters.context: Native isolated BBS role exercise · C-0050-P-20261005 · synthetic October 2026 work only
paragraphs: Actual is saved work. Expected is a planning target. Difference is actual minus expected. Needs note can remain on approved days whose actual hours differ from the target: October 13 shows actual 1 h, expected 8 h and difference −7 h.

There is no weekly control that promises to clear Needs note. Record a truthful explanation in the source activity or correction reason where appropriate; that text may not remove the calculated indicator.
Copy previous week layout prepares draft structure; it never proves that copied work occurred. This copy action was source-checked, not executed in this exercise.
steps: Open week 2026-10-12 and inspect dates, actual, expected, difference and source states.

Before Submit this week, identify every eligible draft and its actual work. The native October 12–18 exercise included ordinary draft 01a1117a-ab69-72fe-9fe3-d618ef3ac078 and linked correction draft 01a1117a-6cef-7576-900b-329b43e9ecb0, both version 1.

Choose Submit this week. Verify success and reopen both sources: each became Submitted. Owner subsequently approved both. The returned original stayed Needs changes and an already approved October 14 row was excluded.
checks: Native eligibility count was 2 and both exact source IDs changed state successfully; count alone was not treated as proof.
recovery: Do not manufacture eight hours to match Expected. Resolve actual source errors with a linked correction; explain a genuine short day truthfully.

figures.caption: Approved actual time still shows Needs note where the expected target differs.
Before: eligible ordinary and linked correction drafts in the displayed week.
After weekly submission: both exact sources became Submitted; later Owner approval is shown separately.

chapters.title: Record an own purchase with its private receipt
chapters.context: Isolated BBS supplier role lab · genuine External Technician account · fictional October 2026 records
paragraphs: The worked expense is explicitly synthetic USD 8 tools/consumables on October 7, Worker payer. The receipt states no real purchase or payment. Your purchase facts are visible to you; Finance classification, customer recovery and reimbursement are later distinct decisions.
The actual form accepts JPG/PNG/HEIC/PDF receipt evidence up to 10 MB. Preserve the original currency and payer. A registered upload is not a universal assertion that an antivirus scan completed.
steps: Choose Record expense. Attach Receipt image or PDF; select Project, Date and Category. Enter Vendor, Amount 8, Currency USD, Who paid Worker and factual Description; fill applicable time/related-hours/payment context.
Use Save draft and open the saved expense. Check the registered receipt and purchase fields.
Use Submit. Genuine PM operationally approved this expense. Open private receipt now succeeds through your own authorized account.
checks: One USD 8 expense and one receipt exist. No Finance review, reimbursement payment or client invoice is claimed for this External exercise.
recovery: If receipt access or scan processing fails, report the document/expense ID and exact status. Do not create another expense while checking the first. Reviewed expense corrections follow the current permitted correction/handoff process.

Own purchase Submitted, then PM Approved; financial treatment is separate.

chapters.title: Write and submit your own daily field report
chapters.context: Isolated BBS supplier role lab · genuine External Technician account · fictional October 2026 records
paragraphs: Daily reports record operational facts, not timesheet hours, supplier payment or customer acceptance. This report’s author is the genuine External Technician account. Its fictional summary says no live equipment.

Fields include Project, Work date, Site / shift, Shift summary, Tasks completed, Problems found, Corrective actions, Downtime minutes, Standby reason, Open items, Next day plan and safety impact. Include genuine problems and next steps; do not invent a successful outcome.
steps: Choose New daily report and fill the actual work date/project and factual summary/tasks. Fill relevant operational exceptions and next steps.
Use Save daily report. Open the Draft and inspect saved contents. Autosaving or saving edits does not submit.
Use Submit for review. Confirm Submitted and the permitted reviewer’s later state.
checks: Own Daily progressed Draft→Submitted→Approved through genuine PM review. It did not add hours or record a customer signature.
recovery: Edit only through offered unsent-draft controls. For returned/approved content, preserve history and use a supported correction or reviewer handoff.

figures.caption: Native own Daily input in the role lab.
Own Daily after separate submission and genuine PM operational approval; ready output is a later step.

chapters.title: Save technical facts and private evidence before submission
chapters.context: Native isolated BBS role exercise · C-0050-P-20261005 · synthetic October 2026 work only
paragraphs: Record system identity, observed issue, diagnosis, change, validation result, production impact, open risks and rollback. The October 19 example is an offline synthetic documentation bench; it claims no live PLC change.
Private evidence is a separate saved attachment. Scan status describes processing; Storage Saved and Scan Not scanned do not mean a clean security scan.
steps: Choose Technical / PLC, your BBS project and Report date 2026-10-19. Complete the technical fields and Save draft.
In private evidence select Evidence type Technical attachment, choose File and enter Notes explaining the evidence and scope. Choose Upload private evidence.
Before Submit verify the listed filename, attachment version, size, hash, Storage Saved and scan status. In this exercise upload preceded submission.
Submit the saved report. Reopen the exact source after PM review and check Approved, work author, report creator, reviewer and source version.
checks: Native report 01a11186-932c-7459-84fb-791179b96c66 reached Approved v3. Its attachment was registered at v2 before Submit. Evidence types available in this Technical form also include PLC backup · before and PLC backup · after.
recovery: If an upload fails, verify whether metadata exists before retrying. Keep backups and customer evidence private; never infer scan success from an upload success.

chapters.title: Generate, check and download the saved report version
chapters.context: Native isolated BBS role exercise · C-0050-P-20261005 · synthetic October 2026 work only
paragraphs: The native preview reflects saved source data. A generated PDF is tied to source version and language; it does not approve the source or certify customer acceptance.
steps: Open your saved report and inspect its native preview. Select English, Spanish or Portuguese, then choose Generate report.
Queued means the artifact is being prepared. Use Refresh until the exact version/language becomes Ready; do not treat Queued as downloadable completion.
Choose Download on the Ready variant. Check project, report date, author, version, language and technical facts against the source.
checks: October 19 Technical source v3 was generated in English, became Ready and was downloaded natively as Technical-report-C-0050-P-20261005-2026-10-19-SYNTHETIC-ET06-documentation-bench-v3-en-US.pdf.
recovery: If a PDF is stale after a source change, generate the new saved version and compare its identity. Preserve prior version history.

figures.caption: Readable native Technical document preview from saved facts.
Ready English v3 variant with native Download.

chapters.title: Reconcile an exact period with its native CSV
chapters.route: Operational report → date filters → Download CSV
chapters.context: Native isolated BBS role exercise · C-0050-P-20261005 · synthetic October 2026 work only
paragraphs: The earlier 2.75 h total is a historical October 6–7 checkpoint, not the current full-month total. Later October records were added. Use exact dates to reproduce it.

The final October 6–7 export contains two Approved rows: 120 minutes on October 6, source 01a10e4b-c33e-7033-a065-d3980b92c94d, and the 45-minute October 7 correction 01a10e53-31a7-7509-86a4-7a134a731e6c. Total 165 minutes = 2.75 h. The returned 60-minute original is not counted as approved work.
steps: Open Operational report, select BBS and filter From 2026-10-06 to To 2026-10-07.
Check technician, dates, duration, State and Recorded by. Choose Download CSV and compare the two exported rows with the filtered screen.
For later work choose a new date range and describe its actual total; never carry the historical 2.75 h forward.
checks: Native final CSV external-final-oct06-07.csv has two Approved rows and nine operational columns. No rate, internal cost, margin or pay column is present.
recovery: If screen and CSV differ, check filters and source states before escalating. Keep both the historical checkpoint and later export identity.

figures.caption: Exact October 6–7 final filtered screen: two Approved rows totaling 2.75 h, matching the final native CSV.

chapters.title: Use narrow screens and check saved results
chapters.context: Isolated BBS supplier role lab · genuine External Technician account · fictional October 2026 records
paragraphs: Use role navigation and narrow-screen menu controls. Review account/project/date/member fields carefully before saving. A table’s internal horizontal-scroll hint is different from page-level overflow.
steps: On a phone open the required workspace through navigation and apply the intended scope.
After saving or submitting, reopen the existing source to verify its result rather than repeating the action.
checks: Operational report checked at 390 and 768 pixels: page width of the scrollable page matches viewport width; native two-source report retained. Desktop 1440 was also inspected.

chapters.title: Maintain your workforce profile and individual security
chapters.route: Profile → Expertise and availability; Account security
chapters.context: Reference procedure · current own-role controls/source checked; mutations not exercised
paragraphs: Expertise and availability are planning inputs, distinct from supplier authorization/project assignment. The own profile was inspected natively; no security or profile mutations occurred here. A generic workforce-profile Worker label does not grant internal Worker financial workspaces.

Add expertise offers expertise/proficiency. Add availability opens dated UTC availability windows. Passkey registration uses Device name and Register passkey. Authenticator setup/recovery material is sensitive; never include it in report evidence.
For invitation and sign-in use Access · activate the invitation and sign in (access). For MFA, devices and recovery use Security · verify your own device and recovery options (security).
steps: Check your own expertise and UTC calendar. Use offered own-profile controls only for genuine information.
For an authorized account-security change use your own device/authenticator prompts and verify completion before signing out. Store recovery codes in an approved password manager.
checks: Skills/availability do not grant review, supplier administration, private-pay or billing rights. Security success is not claimed from read-only controls.
recovery: Ask the Owner/coordinator for authorization/assignment changes and Owner/support for access recovery. Do not share credentials.

figures.caption: Own workforce profile inspected without generating any security secret.

chapters.title: Use Help and hand problems to the correct role
chapters.context: Isolated BBS supplier role lab · genuine External Technician account · fictional October 2026 records
paragraphs: Help’s invitation lesson distinguishes mailbox-linked access and a single-use external invitation; there is no public signup. Supplier operations guidance has different paths for technician/coordinator.

The verified support contact is admin@j-aautomation.com. Live company portal/webmail links are live services. No email was sent in this exercise. External Technician has no My Pay workspace: supplier commercial/payment questions belong to the coordinator/Finance using their authorized process.
steps: Read the External technician starting path and normal-day guidance in Help.
Send actual source errors to the operational reviewer; supplier authorization/account questions to Owner/coordinator; financial issues to coordinator/Finance.
Include environment, role, project/record ID, date, intended action and exact message. Use safe screenshots without session cookies/passwords/recovery codes.
checks: My Pay, Finance, Billing, supplier team and another Worker’s time returned 403. Unrelated report/receipt returned 404 after the own-output route fix.
recovery: Do not use another account to work around denial or publish private receipt links. Marking/reading a notification, where offered, is not approval or acceptance.

chapters.title: Planning appendix · assignment dates and expected targets
chapters.route: Sign in → Time → Week of → Open week
chapters.context: Isolated BBS planning lab · real role browser sessions · fictional October 22–23, 2026 work · no production records or financial changes
paragraphs: Project membership gives dated access to record work; a published plan describes intended work; Expected in the weekly timesheet comes from the effective working schedule. These are three separate records. None creates actual hours, approval, customer charges or pay automatically.

The Owner published a two-hour October 22 assignment for this External Technician. Publishing succeeded, but this restricted profile has no Today agenda or Planning calendar. Sign-in/root opens Time; navigation contains Time, Expenses, Reports, Operational report, Profile and Help. Direct Today and Planning links show Access restricted. This is the current profile limitation, not proof of an absent project assignment.

The effective schedule sets eight expected weekday hours. Our technician separately saved and submitted two fictional actual hours on October 22. The weekly row therefore shows Actual 2.00h, Expected 8.00h and Difference −6.00h, even though the published plan is two hours. The later coordinator-recorded October 23 hour contributes another one hour to the weekly total.

After Owner approval, the weekly status reads Needs note because actual differs from expected; the underlying source remains Approved. It is a schedule-variance prompt, not a rejection, payment state or instruction to invent six missing hours. Ask the Owner how to explain the genuine difference.
steps: Sign in with your own External Technician account and confirm the training environment. Open Time; verify BBS is available in Assigned project before entering work.
For this exercise set Week of to 2026-10-19 and choose Open week. Inspect the October 22 daily row and open its day entries to inspect the actual source separately.

If the Owner tells you a plan was published, obtain the operational time/site instructions through the approved coordinator or Owner communication channel. This profile cannot inspect or accept the internal agenda card.
Record only work actually performed through Log time → Save draft → individual Submit. Check the source becomes Submitted, then Approved after authorized J&A Owner review.
Compare Actual, Expected and Difference. The eight-hour schedule target is not changed by a two-hour plan or by submission.
checks: Native own two-hour save/submission and subsequent Owner approval succeeded. The Owner-created plan remained a separate published record.
External Operational report on October 23 totals only the technician’s own one hour; coordinator’s team report totals two hours. Another technician’s known source returned Access restricted.
Client rates, company cost, margin, supplier payment and colleagues’ compensation are outside this operational workspace.
recovery: If BBS is missing, send the Owner/coordinator your intended project and work date. They must check active account, supplier association, supplier authorization and dated project assignment. Do not borrow a login or duplicate sources.
If Planning or Today is unavailable, return to Time. Creating another assignment or repeatedly requesting the denied page does not add the restricted agenda feature.

An unavailable Expected value is displayed as — when a usable effective schedule/unique assignment cannot be determined. Ask the Owner to investigate scope and dates; do not treat it as zero actual work.

chapters.title: Describe completed work, open goals and the next shift
chapters.route: Reports → New daily report → Save daily report → Submit for review
chapters.context: Isolated BBS planning lab · real role browser sessions · fictional October 22–23, 2026 work · no production records or financial changes
paragraphs: There is no separate worker-goal screen with Accept, Reject or Mark completed buttons. Use operational Daily report fields to describe completed work, unresolved items and intended next steps. A next-day plan is narrative context; it does not publish a shift, create actual time or guarantee a task was done.

The October 22 synthetic report describes a fictional wiring-list review under Tasks completed, a diagram requiring clarification under Open items and a conditional follow-up under Next-day plan. It was saved, submitted and operationally approved by the genuine Project Manager. No customer acceptance, equipment change or payment is asserted.

Time and Daily reports have separate handoffs in this supplier profile. Submitted supplier time is reviewed by an authorized J&A Owner; the ordinary Project Manager Time queue excludes supplier hours. The Project Manager successfully reviewed this Daily report in the Reports queue.
steps: Open Reports and choose New daily report. Select BBS and Work date 2026-10-22; provide Site / shift and Shift summary.

Fill Tasks completed with what happened, Open items with remaining questions and Next-day plan with proposed work. Keep private rates, costs, pay and client-commercial arrangements out of operational narratives.
Choose Save daily report, reopen the new source and inspect the saved fields and Work performed by / Report created by attribution.
Choose Submit for review. Saving alone leaves a draft. After reviewer action refresh and verify Approved.
When the plan or facts change, coordinate with the Owner and use the supported linked correction for a reviewed report. Do not overwrite approved history or invent a task-completion control.
checks: Native save → Submit for review → PM Approve report completed. The approved report retains Tasks completed, Open items and Next-day plan.
The separate two-hour actual source is Owner Approved. Narrative tasks did not create or alter its duration.
recovery: If a time reviewer cannot find supplier hours in the PM queue, hand the exact project, work date and source ID to an authorized J&A Owner; do not submit duplicate time.
Approval is operational review. Continue the separate customer sign-off or financial process only through an authorized role.

figures.caption: Saved approved operational facts: Tasks completed, Open items and Next-day plan. These narrative goals do not create planning or actual-time records.
Same synthetic Daily source after genuine PM approval. Its Approved badge is separate from time approval and customer acceptance.

chapters.title: Complete the technician handoff
chapters.context: Isolated BBS supplier role lab · genuine External Technician account · fictional October 2026 records
paragraphs: Use this task checklist for genuine authorized work in your own account. Saved, submitted, approved, financially reviewed and paid are separate states.
steps: Verify own account/environment/project/date authorization.
Record actual hours once; inspect and submit. Read returned reasons and use linked corrections.
Record each purchase once with actual payer/currency/private evidence; submit for operational review.
Save and submit required Daily/Technical facts; hand risks/open work to PM.
Check review states and current own operational totals; download permitted output only when Ready.
Give reviewer/coordinator source IDs and unresolved issues; never claim customer acceptance/pay from operational approval.
checks: Native coverage includes saved first-shift time, linked correction and Owner approval, ordinary plus correction weekly submission with exact IDs, private Technical upload before Submit, PM Technical approval, Ready English PDF download and exact filtered historical CSV. See Verification · current coverage and historical evidence (verification).
recovery: Layout copying, browser print completion and new customer acceptance remain reference-only. Use the shared access/security chapters for their verified procedures.
